traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md defines a rule that validates @story and @req annotation format and syntax, including multiline handling, flexible parsing, specific error messages, and documentation.
All key requirements are implemented and verified: - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION & REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION: The `valid-annotation-format` rule and its helpers define explicit regex-based formats for @story and @req, apply them to collapsed values, and are thoroughly tested in `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` (both valid and invalid cases). - REQ-PATH-FORMAT: `validateStoryAnnotation` uses a storyPattern regex to enforce `docs/stories/-DEV-.story.md` structure, detects missing values, invalid extensions, traversal (`../`), and applies safe suffix-only autofix where appropriate. Tests cover all these cases, matching the examples from the story. - REQ-REQ-FORMAT: `validateReqAnnotation` enforces a default `^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$` pattern, with configuration support; tests cover missing IDs, invalid formats, and configurable patterns/examples. - REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT: `PendingAnnotation` state, `processCommentLine`, and `finalizePendingAnnotation` handle annotations split across multiple lines, collapsing whitespace before validation. Tests explicitly exercise multi-line story/req cases, and the perf test builds many multi-line JSDoc comments. - REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: `normalizeCommentLine` supports inline/block/JSDoc comments and detects tags anywhere in a line; the rule scans all comments from the Program node. Tests confirm behavior with various spacings and comment styles, and the perf test asserts performance on a large, mixed corpus. - REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY: Error messages are centralized via `invalidStoryFormat`/`invalidReqFormat` and helpers `buildStoryErrorMessage`/`buildReqErrorMessage`, and tests assert the exact message strings, including offending values and expected examples.
Acceptance criteria are satisfied: - Core Functionality: The ESLint rule validates @story/@req (and @supports) formats as specified, with comprehensive passing tests. - Quality Standards: The rule uses ESLint recommended patterns (meta, messages, schema, RuleTester tests) and is integrated into the plugin. - Integration: It operates over all comments at the Program level, so it validates the same annotations used by the function and branch rules, and is included in documented configs. - User Experience: Error messages are clear, specific, and tested to match detailed guidance. - Error Handling: Handles malformed comments, missing values, and invalid regex configurations gracefully (reporting configuration errors and falling back to defaults instead of crashing), with tests for these paths. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents formats, options, and examples of valid/invalid annotations, aligned with the story examples.
All relevant tests (including those explicitly tied to this story) pass in the current test run, so this story is fully implemented.
